operations.name: Clare Schaeffer-Duffy

expected.name: Clare Schaeffer-Duffy
expected.description: Clare Schaeffer-Duffy is a Worcester, Massachusetts Catholic Worker, journalist, and peace organizer. She and her family have lived and worked at Saints Francis and Therese Catholic Worker, operated a community bakery and house of hospitality, and organized nonviolent resistance to war and nuclear weapons. She also organizes with the Center for Nonviolent Solutions. Schaeffer-Duffy was arrested and released after a March 27, 2026 peace witness at the Pentagon.

operations.source: Primary employer/team profile: https://www.nonviolentsolutions.org/team-2/ . Identifies Claire Schaeffer-Duffy, Center for Nonviolent Solutions program director, wife of Scott and co-founder of Worcester SS.Francis and Therese Catholic Worker, matching the stored biography named Clare. Original300x300 portrait downloaded unchanged; no redraw or crop. Existing display-name spelling preserved. See CREDITS-batch893.md.

operations.name: Samantha Frances Brooks

expected.charges: 18 U.S.C. § 1992(a)(5) — terrorist attacks and other violence against railroad carriers.
expected.sentence:
Six months in federal prison, four months of home confinement, three years of supervised release and 200 hours of community service, imposed October 2021 — lighter than co-defendant Ellen Reiche received. Bureau of Prisons register number 19550-509; released May 20, 2022, the date the BOP inmate locator gives as the point she was no longer in Bureau custody. NO ADMISSION DATE TO BUREAU CUSTODY IS DOCUMENTED, so the imprisonment counter stays empty: six months counted back from the release would fall around November 19, 2021, but that is arithmetic rather than evidence. The record previously ran a single span from the November 2020 arrest to May 2022 and counted 538 days, which cannot be right — she pleaded guilty in July 2021 and was sentenced that October, and had she been held from the arrest her credit would have exceeded the six-month term before it was even imposed. She was released pending trial after the arrest; the length of that first custody is not documented. The four months of home confinement are not counted as imprisonment.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — guilty plea, July 2021; sentenced October 2021.

Charges as recorded: 18 U.S.C. § 1992(a)(5) — terrorist attacks and other violence against railroad carriers, for placing a shunting device on BNSF Railway track near Bellingham, Washington on November 28, 2020 with Ellen Reiche, in solidarity with the Wetsuweten hereditary chiefs opposing pipeline construction in British Columbia.

operations.source: Primary DOJ report December17,2021 individually distinguishes Brooks from co-defendant Reiche, expressly gives July9 guilty plea and October2021 sentencing: https://www.justice.gov/usao-wdwa/pr/bellingham-washington-woman-sentenced-prison-shunt-attack-bnsf-track . Sentencing MONTH precision only. Exact October8 lead appears in railway-industry reporting but no executed court record inspected to independently narrow it. No admission from sentence or BOP release arithmetic.

operations.name: Paul Nakadate

expected.sentence:
Four years at the U.S. Penitentiary, Leavenworth; the convictions were reversed on appeal in 1945.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted by a federal jury in Cheyenne in October 1944 and sentenced to four years at Leavenworth; the Tenth Circuit overturned the conspiracy convictions in 1945.

Charges as recorded: Conspiracy to counsel draft evasion — for leading the Heart Mountain Fair Play Committee, which urged imprisoned Nisei to refuse induction until their constitutional rights as U.S. citizens were restored.

operations.source: Court historical timeline of the Heart Mountain draft-resister trial: https://justiceforall.ca2.uscourts.gov/reenactments/heart-mountain-draft-resisters/the-heart-mountain-draft-resisters-timeline/ . Individual museum profile confirms Nakadate among convicted leaders: https://heartmountain.org/draft-resisters-hub/nakadate-paul-takeo/ . Primary judgment-and-commitment dating corroborated by National Archives for this joint case: https://text-message.blogs.archives.gov/2022/06/07/japanese-american-internment-and-resistance-at-heart-mountain/ . Administrative internment, later arrest, prison transfer and appellate reversal remain distinct; no first prison entry assigned from sentencing.
